# Reference
## History
<details><summary><code>client.history.<a href="/src/api/resources/history/history.rs">list</a>(request: &amp;ListQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;GetSpeechHistoryResponse, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Returns a list of your generated audio (e.g. text to speech, speech to speech, Studio, dubbing). Music and SFX generations are not included and cannot currently be retrieved via the API.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .history
        .list(
            &ListQueryRequest {
                page_size: Some(100),
                start_after_history_item_id: Some("start_after_history_item_id".to_string()),
                voice_id: Some("voice_id".to_string()),
                model_id: Some("model_id".to_string()),
                date_before_unix: Some(8),
                date_after_unix: Some(2),
                sort_direction: Some(BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPostSort::Asc),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                source: Some(ListSource::Tts),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&ListQueryRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.page_size:** `Option<i64>` — How many history items to return at maximum. Can not exceed 1000, defaults to 100.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.start_after_history_item_id:** `Option<String>` — After which ID to start fetching, use this parameter to paginate across a large collection of history items. In case this parameter is not provided history items will be fetched starting from the most recently created one ordered descending by their creation date.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.voice_id:** `Option<String>` — ID of the voice to be filtered for. You can use the [Get voices](/docs/api-reference/voices/search) endpoint list all the available voices.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.model_id:** `Option<String>` — Search term used for filtering history items. If provided, source becomes required.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.date_before_unix:** `Option<i64>` — Unix timestamp to filter history items before this date (exclusive).
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.date_after_unix:** `Option<i64>` — Unix timestamp to filter history items after this date (inclusive).
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort_direction:** `Option<BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPostSort>` — Sort direction for the results.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.search:** `Option<String>` — search term used for filtering
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.source:** `Option<ListSource>` — Source of the generated history item
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.history.<a href="/src/api/resources/history/history.rs">download</a>(body: &amp;DownloadHistoryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;crate::core::ByteStream, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Download one or more history items. If one history item ID is provided, we will return a single audio file. If more than one history item IDs are provided, we will provide the history items packed into a .zip file.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .history
        .download(
            &DownloadHistoryRequest::builder()
                .history_item_ids(vec!["history_item_ids".to_string()])
                .output_format("output_format")
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

## TextToSoundEffects
<details><summary><code>client.text_to_sound_effects.<a href="/src/api/resources/text_to_sound_effects/text_to_sound_effects.rs">convert</a>(request: &amp;ConvertRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;crate::core::ByteStream, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Turn text into sound effects for your videos, voice-overs or video games using the most advanced sound effects models in the world.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .text_to_sound_effects
        .convert(
            &ConvertRequest::builder()
                .output_format(ConvertOutputFormatQueryParameter1::Alaw8000)
                .enable_logging(true)
                .body(
                    CreateSoundEffectRequest::builder()
                        .text("Spacious braam suitable for high-impact movie trailer moments")
                        .r#loop(true)
                        .duration_seconds(8.36)
                        .prompt_influence(6.22)
                        .model_id(SfxModelId::ElevenTextToSoundV2)
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                )
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&ConvertRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.output_format:** `Option<ConvertOutputFormatQueryParameter1>` — Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM and WAV formats with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.enable_logging:** `Option<bool>` — When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.body:** `CreateSoundEffectRequest`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

## TextToSpeech
<details><summary><code>client.text_to_speech.<a href="/src/api/resources/text_to_speech/text_to_speech.rs">convert</a>(voice_id: &amp;str, request: &amp;TextToSpeechConvertRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;crate::core::ByteStream, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Converts text into speech using a voice of your choice and returns audio.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .text_to_speech
        .convert(
            "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
            &TextToSpeechConvertRequest::builder()
                .enable_logging(true)
                .optimize_streaming_latency(10)
                .output_format(ConvertOutputFormatQueryParameter1::Mp3_44100_128)
                .body(
                    BodyTextToSpeechFull::builder()
                        .text("The first move is what sets everything in motion.")
                        .model_id("eleven_multilingual_v2")
                        .language_code("language_code")
                        .voice_settings(BodyTextToSpeechFullVoiceSettings {
                            stability: Some(0.62),
                            use_speaker_boost: Some(true),
                            similarity_boost: Some(0.18),
                            style: Some(2.67),
                            speed: Some(5.4),
                            clone_strength: Some(0.53),
                            ..Default::default()
                        })
                        .pronunciation_dictionary_locators(vec![
                            BodyTextToSpeechFullPronunciationDictionaryLocators::builder()
                                .pronunciation_dictionary_id("pronunciation_dictionary_id")
                                .version_id("version_id")
                                .build()
                                .expect("Failed to build request"),
                        ])
                        .seed(1)
                        .previous_text("previous_text")
                        .next_text("next_text")
                        .previous_request_ids(vec!["previous_request_ids".to_string()])
                        .next_request_ids(vec!["next_request_ids".to_string()])
                        .use_pvc_as_ivc(false)
                        .apply_text_normalization(
                            BodyTextToDialogueFullWithTimestampsApplyTextNormalization::Auto,
                        )
                        .audio_effects(EffectsSpecInput {
                            filter_preset_id: Some("filter_preset_id".to_string()),
                            distance: Some(0.89),
                            environment_id: Some("environment_id".to_string()),
                            background_noise_id: Some("background_noise_id".to_string()),
                            send_level: Some(1_f64),
                            pan: Some(-0.33),
                            ..Default::default()
                        })
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                )
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**voice_id:** `&str` — ID of the voice to be used. Use the [Get voices](/docs/api-reference/voices/search) endpoint list all the available voices.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&TextToSpeechConvertRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.enable_logging:** `Option<bool>` — When enable_logging is set to false zero retention mode will be used for the request. This will mean history features are unavailable for this request, including request stitching. Zero retention mode may only be used by enterprise customers.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.optimize_streaming_latency:** `Option<i64>` 

You can turn on latency optimizations at some cost of quality. The best possible final latency varies by model. Possible values:
0 - default mode (no latency optimizations)
1 - normal latency optimizations (about 50% of possible latency improvement of option 3)
2 - strong latency optimizations (about 75% of possible latency improvement of option 3)
3 - max latency optimizations
4 - max latency optimizations, but also with text normalizer turned off for even more latency savings (best latency, but can mispronounce eg numbers and dates).

Defaults to None.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.output_format:** `Option<ConvertOutputFormatQueryParameter1>` — Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM and WAV formats with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.body:** `BodyTextToSpeechFull`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

2 - strong latency optimizations (about 75% of possible latency improvement of option 3)
3 - max latency optimizations
4 - max latency optimizations, but also with text normalizer turned off for even more latency savings (best latency, but can mispronounce eg numbers and dates).

Defaults to None.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.output_format:** `Option<StreamOutputFormatQueryParameter1>` — Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.body:** `BodyTextToSpeechStream`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.text_to_speech.<a href="/src/api/resources/text_to_speech/text_to_speech.rs">stream_with_timestamps</a>(voice_id: &amp;str, request: &amp;StreamWithTimestampsRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;crate::SseStream&lt;StreamingAudioChunkWithTimestampsResponse&gt;, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Converts text into speech using a voice of your choice and returns a stream of JSONs containing audio as a base64 encoded string together with information on when which character was spoken.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;
use futures::StreamExt;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    let mut stream = client
        .text_to_speech
        .stream_with_timestamps(
            "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
            &StreamWithTimestampsRequest::builder()
                .enable_logging(true)
                .optimize_streaming_latency(8)
                .output_format(StreamOutputFormatQueryParameter1::Mp3_44100_128)
                .body(
                    BodyTextToSpeechStreamWithTimestamps::builder()
                        .text("The first move is what sets everything in motion.")
                        .model_id("eleven_multilingual_v2")
                        .language_code("language_code")
                        .voice_settings(BodyTextToSpeechFullVoiceSettings {
                            stability: Some(0.62),
                            use_speaker_boost: Some(true),
                            similarity_boost: Some(0.18),
                            style: Some(2.67),
                            speed: Some(5.4),
                            clone_strength: Some(0.53),
                            ..Default::default()
                        })
                        .pronunciation_dictionary_locators(vec![
                            BodyTextToSpeechFullPronunciationDictionaryLocators::builder()
                                .pronunciation_dictionary_id("pronunciation_dictionary_id")
                                .version_id("version_id")
                                .build()
                                .expect("Failed to build request"),
                        ])
                        .seed(4)
                        .previous_text("previous_text")
                        .next_text("next_text")
                        .previous_request_ids(vec!["previous_request_ids".to_string()])
                        .next_request_ids(vec!["next_request_ids".to_string()])
                        .use_pvc_as_ivc(false)
                        .apply_text_normalization(
                            BodyTextToDialogueFullWithTimestampsApplyTextNormalization::Auto,
                        )
                        .audio_effects(EffectsSpecInput {
                            filter_preset_id: Some("filter_preset_id".to_string()),
                            distance: Some(0.89),
                            environment_id: Some("environment_id".to_string()),
                            background_noise_id: Some("background_noise_id".to_string()),
                            send_level: Some(1_f64),
                            pan: Some(-0.33),
                            ..Default::default()
                        })
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                )
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await
        .expect("Request failed");
    while let Some(item) = stream.next().await {
        println!("{:?}", item.expect("Failed to read stream item"));
    }
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.

<details><summary><code>client.voices.<a href="/src/api/resources/voices/voices.rs">search</a>(request: &amp;SearchQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;GetVoicesV2Response, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Gets a list of all available voices for a user with search, filtering and pagination.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .voices
        .search(
            &SearchQueryRequest {
                next_page_token: Some("next_page_token".to_string()),
                page_size: Some(10),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                sort: Some("sort".to_string()),
                sort_direction: Some("sort_direction".to_string()),
                voice_type: Some("voice_type".to_string()),
                category: Some("category".to_string()),
                fine_tuning_state: Some("fine_tuning_state".to_string()),
                collection_id: Some("collection_id".to_string()),
                gender: Some("gender".to_string()),
                age: Some("age".to_string()),
                language: Some(vec![]),
                accent: Some("accent".to_string()),
                use_cases: Some(vec![]),
                min_notice_period_days: Some(1),
                include_custom_rates: Some(false),
                include_live_moderated: Some(true),
                high_quality: Some(false),
                include_total_count: Some(true),
                voice_ids: Some(vec![]),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&SearchQueryRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.next_page_token:** `Option<String>` — The next page token to use for pagination. Returned from the previous request. Use this in combination with the has_more flag for reliable pagination.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.page_size:** `Option<i64>` — How many voices to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 10. Page 0 may include more voices due to default voices being included.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.search:** `Option<String>` — Search term to filter voices by. Searches in name, description, labels, category.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort:** `Option<String>` — Which field to sort by, one of 'created_at_unix' or 'name'. 'created_at_unix' may not be available for older voices.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort_direction:** `Option<String>` — Which direction to sort the voices in. 'asc' or 'desc'.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.voice_type:** `Option<String>` — Type of the voice to filter by. One of 'personal', 'community', 'default', 'workspace', 'non-default', 'non-community', 'saved'. 'non-default' is equal to all but 'default'. 'non-community' is equal to 'personal' and 'workspace' combined (excludes library copies). 'saved' is equal to non-default, but includes default voices if they have been added to a collection.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.category:** `Option<String>` — Category of the voice to filter by. One of 'premade', 'cloned', 'generated', 'professional'
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.fine_tuning_state:** `Option<String>` — State of the voice's fine tuning to filter by. Applicable only to professional voices clones. One of 'draft', 'not_verified', 'not_started', 'queued', 'fine_tuning', 'fine_tuned', 'failed', 'delayed'
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.collection_id:** `Option<String>` — Collection ID to filter voices by.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.gender:** `Option<String>` — Gender used for filtering, based on the voice's 'gender' label.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.age:** `Option<String>` — Age used for filtering, based on the voice's 'age' label.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.language:** `Option<Vec<String>>` — Languages used for filtering, based on the voice's 'language' label. Voices matching any of the given languages are returned.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.accent:** `Option<String>` — Accent used for filtering, based on the voice's 'accent' label.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.use_cases:** `Option<Vec<String>>` — Use cases used for filtering, based on the voice's 'use_case' label. Voices matching any of the given use cases are returned.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.min_notice_period_days:** `Option<i64>` — Filter to voices whose sharing notice period is at least the given number of days.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.include_custom_rates:** `Option<bool>` — Whether to include voices that have a custom sharing rate. Defaults to including them.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.include_live_moderated:** `Option<bool>` — Whether to include voices that have live moderation enabled. Defaults to including them.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.high_quality:** `Option<bool>` — When true, only return studio-quality voices (those whose category is 'high_quality').
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.include_total_count:** `Option<bool>` — Whether to include the total count of voices found in the response. NOTE: The total_count value is a live snapshot and may change between requests as users create, modify, or delete voices. For pagination, rely on the has_more flag instead. Only enable this when you actually need the total count (e.g., for display purposes), as it incurs a performance cost.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.voice_ids:** `Option<Vec<String>>` — Voice IDs to lookup by. Maximum 100 voice IDs.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.voices.<a href="/src/api/resources/voices/voices.rs">replicate_to_isolated_environment</a>(voice_id: &amp;str, body: &amp;ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentRequestModel, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Replicates an Instant Voice Clone or Voice Design voice to a workspace in a different data residency. The target workspace must belong to the same consolidated billing group. The user must have VOICES_WRITE in the source workspace, and be an admin on the source voice. Human users (i.e. not service accounts) must also have VOICES_WRITE in the target workspace. This endpoint is available on the central environment only.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .voices
        .replicate_to_isolated_environment(
            "21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM",
            &ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentRequestModel::builder()
                .target_workspace_id("target_workspace_id")
                .preserve_voice_id(true)
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**voice_id:** `&str` — Voice ID to be used, you can use https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices to list all the available voices.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**body:** `&ReplicateVoiceToIsolatedEnvironmentRequestModel`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>

</dd>
</dl>

</dl>

        .transcript

            "0199a3f0-1c2d-7abc-8def-0123456789ab",
            &DubbingSegmentUpdateRequest {
                text: Some("Welcome to our latest product demo.".to_string()),
                speaker_id: Some("speaker_id".to_string()),
                start_s: Some(2.07),
                end_s: Some(4.59),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}

<details><summary><code>client.transcript.<a href="/src/api/resources/transcript/transcript.rs">create_segment</a>(project_id: &amp;str, body: &amp;DubbingSegmentCreateRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;DubbingSourceSegmentUpdateResponse, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Enterprise only. Add a new source segment to the transcript. Its span must lie within the source media, last between 0.1 and 25 seconds, and not overlap another segment by the same speaker. Bumps the project's `revision`, discards the affected translations in every language target, and marks any target that had already completed `stale`. No audio changes until you regenerate a target.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .transcript
        .create_segment(
            "proj_1601kwkyxp0hfzvtmyxwqxx6mcy3",
            &DubbingSegmentCreateRequest::builder()
                .text("Thanks for watching.")
                .speaker_id("default_speaker")
                .start_s(42_f64)
                .end_s(44_f64)
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

<dd>

                .segments(HashMap::from([
                    (
                        "0199a3f0-1c2d-7abc-8def-0123456789ab".to_string(),

                        },

        )

<details><summary><code>client.transcript.<a href="/src/api/resources/transcript/transcript.rs">regenerate</a>(project_id: &amp;str, language_id: &amp;str, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;DubbingRegenerateResponse, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Enterprise only. Re-dub a target from its edited transcript, re-synthesizing only the edited regions (charged like a generation, less the free-regeneration allowance). Accepted asynchronously: the target returns to `processing` and sends a `dubbing_language_completed` event to the project's `webhook_ids` when the re-dub lands, carrying the new output URLs. Returns a conflict when the target has no edits to apply — nothing is dispatched and nothing is charged.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .transcript
        .regenerate(
            "proj_1601kwkyxp0hfzvtmyxwqxx6mcy3",
            "lang_1001kwkyxp0je6ktn4knsfrasx5s",
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

</dd>

## Workspace
<details><summary><code>client.workspace.<a href="/src/api/resources/workspace/workspace.rs">set_third_party_disabling_policy</a>(body: Option&lt;&amp;BodySetWorkspaceThirdPartyDisablingPolicyV1WorkspacesApiKeysThirdPartyDisablingPost&gt;, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;serde_json::Value, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Set the workspace-wide Third-Party Disabling policy. When set, it forces, for every API key in the workspace, whether the holder of a key (potentially a third party who found it) may disable it via the self-disable endpoint or when it leaks publicly — overriding each key's own setting. Pass `true` to allow it for all keys, `false` to forbid it for all keys, or `null` to clear the override so per-key values and the plan default apply again. Workspace admins only.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .workspace
        .set_third_party_disabling_policy(
            Some(&BodySetWorkspaceThirdPartyDisablingPolicyV1WorkspacesApiKeysThirdPartyDisablingPost {
                third_party_disable_allowed: Some(false),
                ..Default::default()
            }),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>

## Invites
<details><summary><code>client.invites.<a href="/src/api/resources/invites/invites.rs">create</a>(body: &amp;InviteUserRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;AddWorkspaceInviteResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Sends an email invitation to join your workspace to the provided email. If the user doesn't have an account they will be prompted to create one. If the user accepts this invite they will be added as a user to your workspace and your subscription using one of your seats. This endpoint may only be called by workspace members with the WORKSPACE_MEMBERS_INVITE permission. If the user is already in the workspace a 400 error will be returned.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .invites
        .create(
            &InviteUserRequest::builder()
                .email("john.doe@testmail.com")
                .seat_type(SeatType::WorkspaceAdmin)
                .group_ids(vec!["group_ids".to_string()])
                .usage_limit(9)
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Sends email invitations to join your workspace to the provided emails. Requires all email addresses to be part of a verified domain. If the users don't have an account they will be prompted to create one. If the users accept these invites they will be added as users to your workspace and your subscription using one of your seats. This endpoint may only be called by workspace members with the WORKSPACE_MEMBERS_INVITE permission.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

    client
        .invites
        .create_batch(

                .emails(vec!["emails".to_string()])
                .seat_type(SeatType::WorkspaceAdmin)
                .group_ids(vec!["group_ids".to_string()])
                .usage_limit(0)
                .build()

<details><summary><code>client.resources.<a href="/src/api/resources/resources/resources.rs">share</a>(resource_id: &amp;str, body: &amp;BodyShareWorkspaceResourceV1WorkspaceResourcesResourceIdSharePost, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;serde_json::Value, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Grants a role (one of 'admin', 'editor', 'commenter', or 'viewer') on a workspace resource to a user, group, or workspace (service account) API key. This overrides any existing role the target has on the resource. To target a user or service account, pass only the user email; the user must be in your workspace. To target a group, pass only the group id. To target a workspace (service account) API key, pass the api key id; the resource will be shared with the service account associated with that key. You must have admin access to the resource to share it.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

    client
        .resources
        .share(
            "resource_id",
            &BodyShareWorkspaceResourceV1WorkspaceResourcesResourceIdSharePost::builder()
                .role(BodyShareWorkspaceResourceV1WorkspaceResourcesResourceIdSharePostRole::Admin)
                .resource_type(WorkspaceResourceType::Voice)
                .user_email("user_email")
                .group_id("group_id")
                .workspace_api_key_id("workspace_api_key_id")
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}

</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.output_format:** `Option<AllowedOutputFormats>` — Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. MP3 with 192kbps bitrate requires you to be subscribed to Creator tier or above. PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.
    
</dd>

<dl>

<dl>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;
use futures::StreamExt;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    let mut stream = client
        .music
        .compose_detailed_stream(
            &ComposeDetailedStreamRequest {
                output_format: Some(ComposeDetailedOutputFormat::Auto),
                enable_logging: Some(true),
                body: Some(BodyStreamComposedMusicWithADetailedResponseV1MusicDetailedStreamPost {
                    prompt: Some("prompt".to_string()),
                    music_length_ms: Some(512586),
                    model_id: Some(MusicModelId::MusicV1),
                    seed: Some(1289422274),
                    force_instrumental: Some(true),
                    finetune_id: Some("finetune_id".to_string()),
                    store_for_inpainting: Some(true),
                    with_timestamps: Some(true),
                    with_waveform_visual: Some(false),
                    ..Default::default()
                }),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await
        .expect("Request failed");
    while let Some(item) = stream.next().await {

    }
}

PCM with 44.1kHz sample rate requires you to be subscribed to Pro tier or above. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.

## SpeechToText
<details><summary><code>client.speech_to_text.<a href="/src/api/resources/speech_to_text/speech_to_text.rs">convert</a>(body: &amp;BodySpeechToTextV1SpeechToTextPost, request: &amp;SpeechToTextConvertQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;ResponseSpeechToTextV1SpeechToTextPost, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Transcribe an audio or video file. If webhook is set to true, the request will be processed asynchronously and results sent to configured webhooks. When use_multi_channel is true and the provided audio has multiple channels, a 'transcripts' object with separate transcripts for each channel is returned; set multichannel_output_style='combined' to instead receive a single transcript with all channels merged and sorted by time. Otherwise, returns a single transcript. The optional webhook_metadata parameter allows you to attach custom data that will be included in webhook responses for request correlation and tracking.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .speech_to_text
        .convert(
            &BodySpeechToTextV1SpeechToTextPost::builder()
                .model_id("scribe_v2")
                .file(vec![])
                .language_code("language_code")
                .secondary_language_codes(vec!["secondary_language_codes".to_string()])
                .numbers_format(NumbersFormat::Digits)
                .transcript_edit("transcript_edit")
                .tag_audio_events(true)
                .num_speakers(17)
                .timestamps_granularity(
                    BodySpeechToTextV1SpeechToTextPostTimestampsGranularity::None,
                )
                .diarize(false)
                .diarization_threshold(0.16)
                .additional_formats(AdditionalFormats(vec![ExportOptions::Docx {
                    data: DocxExportOptions::builder()
                        .include_speakers(true)
                        .include_timestamps(true)
                        .segment_on_silence_longer_than_s(1.6)
                        .max_segment_duration_s(4.35)
                        .max_segment_chars(7)
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                }]))
                .file_format(FileFormat::PcmS16Le16)
                .source_url("source_url")
                .webhook(false)
                .webhook_id("webhook_id")
                .temperature(1.08)
                .seed(1786060596)
                .use_multi_channel(true)
                .multichannel_output_style(MultichannelOutputStyle::Separate)
                .no_verbatim(true)
                .use_speaker_library(false)
                .detect_speaker_roles(false)
                .entity_redaction_mode("enumerated_entity_type")
                .keyterms(vec!["keyterms".to_string()])
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            &SpeechToTextConvertQueryRequest {
                token: Some("token".to_string()),
                enable_logging: Some(true),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 📝 Description

use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .conversations
        .resolve(
            &ResolveQueryRequest::builder()
                .agent_id("agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz")
                .reference("https://your-domain.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/12345")
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}

<details><summary><code>client.conversations.<a href="/src/api/resources/conversations/conversations.rs">get_summary</a>(conversation_id: &amp;str, request: &amp;GetSummaryQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;GetConversationSummaryResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Get a lightweight summary of a conversation: its title, the generated transcript summary, whether the call was successful, and — only when the conversation is short — the plain chat messages. Tool calls, tool results, and contextual updates are omitted so the response stays small. Use this instead of the full conversation endpoint when you only need the gist (e.g. an agent reading many conversations); use GET /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id} when you need the full transcript with tool calls and contextual updates.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .conversations
        .get_summary(
            "21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM",
            &GetSummaryQueryRequest {
                max_messages: Some(40),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .agents
        .get(
            "agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz",
            &AgentsGetQueryRequest {
                version_id: Some("version_id".to_string()),
                branch_id: Some("branch_id".to_string()),
                include_procedure_generated_workflow_elements: Some(true),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}

use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]

    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .agents
        .delete(
            "agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz",
            &DeleteQueryRequest {
                force: Some(false),
                ..Default::default()
            },

        )
        .await;
}

<details><summary><code>client.agents.<a href="/src/api/resources/agents/agents.rs">duplicate</a>(agent_id: &amp;str, body: Option&lt;&amp;BodyDuplicateAgentV1ConvaiAgentsAgentIdDuplicatePost&gt;, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;CreateAgentResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Create a new agent by duplicating an existing one. The new agent gets a copy of every unarchived branch of the source agent, each with the same name and description and starting from the latest version on that branch. The live traffic split is copied onto the new branches, with any share held by a branch that was not copied moved to main. Version history, drafts, archived branches, past traffic splits and experiments are not copied.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .agents
        .duplicate(
            "agent_3701k3ttaq12ewp8b7qv5rfyszkz",
            Some(&BodyDuplicateAgentV1ConvaiAgentsAgentIdDuplicatePost {
                name: Some("name".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            }),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

    client
        .invocations
        .list(
            &InvocationsListQueryRequest {
                agent_id: Some("agent_id".to_string()),
                branch_id: Some("branch_id".to_string()),
                created_by_user_id: Some("created_by_user_id".to_string()),
                test_id: Some("test_id".to_string()),
                start_time: Some(5),
                end_time: Some(3),
                version_id: Some("version_id".to_string()),
                page_size: Some(30),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                cursor: Some("cursor".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&InvocationsListQueryRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.agent_id:** `Option<String>` — Filter by agent ID
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.branch_id:** `Option<String>` — Filter by branch ID
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.created_by_user_id:** `Option<String>` — Filter by test run creator user ID
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.test_id:** `Option<String>` — Filter to invocations that include a run of this test id
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.start_time:** `Option<i64>` — Inclusive lower bound on created_at, in unix seconds
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.end_time:** `Option<i64>` — Inclusive upper bound on created_at, in unix seconds
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.version_id:** `Option<String>` — Filter by the agent version the tests ran against
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.page_size:** `Option<i64>` — How many Tests to return at maximum. Can not exceed 100, defaults to 30.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.search:** `Option<String>` — Search query to filter tests and folders by name.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.cursor:** `Option<String>` — Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>

<details><summary><code>client.triage_tickets.<a href="/src/api/resources/triage_tickets/triage_tickets.rs">list</a>(agent_id: &amp;str, request: &amp;TriageTicketsListQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;GetAgentConversationTicketsPageResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>

<dd>

List an agent's conversation triage tickets, ordered by most recently created first unless sorted by priority. These are tickets about the agent's own performance on a conversation (for triage with Architect), not tickets an agent opens for end users.
</dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .triage_tickets
        .list(
            "agent_id",
            &TriageTicketsListQueryRequest {
                page_size: Some(100),
                conversation_id: Some("conversation_id".to_string()),
                status: Some(AgentConversationTicketStatus::Open),
                sources: Some(vec![]),
                priorities: Some(vec![]),
                sort_by: Some(AgentConversationTicketSortBy::CreatedAt),
                owner_user_id: Some("owner_user_id".to_string()),
                assignee_user_id: Some("assignee_user_id".to_string()),
                issue_type: Some(AgentConversationTicketIssueType::KnowledgeGap),
                label: Some("label".to_string()),
                merged_into_ticket_id: Some("merged_into_ticket_id".to_string()),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                cursor: Some("cursor".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

List conversation triage tickets across every agent in the workspace, ordered by most recently created first. Use this to build a workspace-wide view (for example, tickets assigned to the caller). Supports the same filters, sorting and search as the per-agent endpoint. Tickets for agents the caller cannot access are omitted.

<dd>

                page_size: Some(100),
                agent_id: Some("agent_id".to_string()),
                status: Some(AgentConversationTicketStatus::Open),
                sources: Some(vec![]),
                priorities: Some(vec![]),
                sort_by: Some(AgentConversationTicketSortBy::CreatedAt),
                owner_user_id: Some("owner_user_id".to_string()),
                assignee_user_id: Some("assignee_user_id".to_string()),
                issue_type: Some(AgentConversationTicketIssueType::KnowledgeGap),
                label: Some("label".to_string()),
                merged_into_ticket_id: Some("merged_into_ticket_id".to_string()),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                cursor: Some("cursor".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}

<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort_by:** `Option<AgentConversationTicketSortBy>` — Order by most recently created, by priority (most urgent first, then most recently created), or by most recently reported (the newest report merged into the issue, else its creation).

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**agent_id:** `&str` — ID of the agent
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&TopicsGetQueryRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.page_size:** `Option<i64>` — Number of top-level topic groups to return.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort_by:** `Option<TopicSortBy>` — Column to rank topics by. Use conversations for volume, sentiment with sort_direction=asc for the most negative topics, and frustration with sort_direction=desc for the most frustrated ones. Topics with no score are always ranked last.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.sort_direction:** `Option<BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPostSort>` — Direction to sort topics.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.from_unix_secs:** `Option<i64>` — Start of the window to view topics for. When set with to_unix_secs, the completed daily topic-discovery runs in the range are aggregated together, so the window scopes the metrics as well as the topic set. Floored to the start of its UTC day because runs cover whole UTC days; aggregated_run_count reports how many runs were summed. Omit both bounds to get the single latest run.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.to_unix_secs:** `Option<i64>` — End of the window to view topics for.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.include_evaluation_criteria:** `Option<bool>` — Include the per-criteria evaluation breakdown on each topic's metrics. Pass false to drop it: it dominates the payload and the weighted success_rate is returned either way.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.cursor:** `Option<String>` — Used for fetching next page. Cursor is returned in the response.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.procedures.<a href="/src/api/resources/procedures/procedures.rs">list</a>(agent_id: &amp;str, branch_id: &amp;str, request: &amp;ProceduresListQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;ListProceduresResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

List the procedures attached to this agent branch. By default, unpublished drafts take precedence over the latest committed version. Pass agent_version_id to list a published snapshot instead. has_draft is true when a procedure has unpublished draft changes on this branch. Procedure content is not included; use Get Procedure to read a procedure's body.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

                agent_version_id: Some("agent_version_id".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,

}

<details><summary><code>client.procedures.<a href="/src/api/resources/procedures/procedures.rs">compile</a>(agent_id: &amp;str, branch_id: &amp;str, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;CompileProceduresResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Legacy. Do not use. Saving an agent draft (`POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/drafts`) and publishing an agent (`PATCH /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}`) compile structured procedures into workflow nodes and edges, save the compiled workflow with the draft or version, and return validation errors, so a separate compile call is no longer needed. This endpoint remains available for the time being so existing callers do not break, as a dry-run that compiles the current procedure drafts into a workflow without persisting anything. It will eventually be deprecated.
</dd>

<dd>

#### 📝 Description

}

                .declared_language("declared_language")
                .media(vec![])

                .media_url_filename("media_url_filename")
                .media_url_content_type("media_url_content_type")

use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .video
        .create(

                    .webhook(WebhookTarget::All {
                        data: WebhookTargetAll::builder().build().expect("Failed to build request"),
                    })
                    .prompt(
                        "A corgi rides a tiny surfboard across a sunlit wave at golden hour, cinematic",
                    )
                    .aspect_ratio(BytedanceSeedance2FastRequestAspectRatio::Auto)
                    .duration_secs(5)
                    .seed(7)
                    .generate_audio(true)
                    .start_frame(ImageReference::Asset {
                        data: StaticAssetReference::builder()
                            .asset_id("5xM2KqOnZyce22SPZ9d4")
                            .build()
                            .expect("Failed to build request"),
                    })
                    .end_frame(ImageReference::Asset {
                        data: StaticAssetReference::builder()
                            .asset_id("5xM2KqOnZyce22SPZ9d4")
                            .build()
                            .expect("Failed to build request"),
                    })
                    .images(vec![ImageReference::Asset {
                        data: StaticAssetReference::builder()
                            .asset_id("5xM2KqOnZyce22SPZ9d4")
                            .build()
                            .expect("Failed to build request"),
                    }])
                    .videos(vec![VideoReference::Asset {
                        data: StaticAssetReference::builder()
                            .asset_id("5xM2KqOnZyce22SPZ9d4")
                            .build()
                            .expect("Failed to build request"),
                    }])
                    .audios(vec![AudioReference::Asset {
                        data: StaticAssetReference::builder()
                            .asset_id("5xM2KqOnZyce22SPZ9d4")
                            .build()
                            .expect("Failed to build request"),
                    }])
                    .resolution(BytedanceSeedance2RequestResolution::Num480P)
                    .build()
                    .expect("Failed to build request"),
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

<details><summary><code>client.runs.<a href="/src/api/resources/runs/runs.rs">create</a>(template_id: &amp;str, body: &amp;TemplateRunCreateRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;TemplateRunResponse, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Start a run of a flows template. Pass `version_id` to pin a snapshot, or omit it / pass `latest` to run the latest published version. Set input values under `inputs`, keyed by input port id. The response is the run in its initial state, with every output already listed under its port id in `outputs`. Include `webhook` to receive a `flows_template_run` event carrying the finished run once its `status` is `completed` or `failed`; this is the recommended way to wait. Without one, fetch `GET /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}/runs/{run_id}` at a modest interval until the `status` is terminal.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .runs
        .create(
            "template_id",
            &TemplateRunCreateRequest::builder()
                .inputs(HashMap::new())
                .version_id("version_id")
                .webhook(WebhookTarget::All {
                    data: WebhookTargetAll::builder().build().expect("Failed to build request"),
                })
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**template_id:** `&str` — The ID of the template, as shown in the ElevenLabs app or by `GET /v1/flows/templates`.

<dl>
<dd>

**body:** `&TemplateRunCreateRequest`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.templates.<a href="/src/api/resources/templates/templates.rs">list</a>(request: &amp;TemplatesListQueryRequest, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;TemplateListResponse, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>

<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

List the published flows templates in your workspace, together with each runnable version's inputs and outputs. Use the ids here as `template_id` / `version_id` on `POST /v1/flows/templates/{template_id}/runs`. Versions built on models that are not available to you through the API are left out, so `versions` is empty when none of a template's published versions is runnable through this API. Templates shared with you by link, or published to Explore from another workspace, are not listed but can still be fetched and run by `template_id`.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .templates
        .list(
            &TemplatesListQueryRequest {
                cursor: Some("cursor".to_string()),
                page_size: Some(10),
                versions_per_template: Some(3),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**request:** `&TemplatesListQueryRequest` — Query parameters for this request
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.cursor:** `Option<String>` — Pagination cursor: the `next_cursor` value of the previous page's response. Omit it for the first page.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.page_size:** `Option<i64>` — How many templates to return per page. Lower than the run list's ceiling because each row expands its versions' input and output schemas.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.versions_per_template:** `Option<i64>` — How many of each template's published versions to return, newest first. `has_more_versions` tells you when a template has more.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**request.search:** `Option<String>` — Only return templates whose name or description contains this text.
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

</dd>

    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .templates
        .get(
            "template_id",
            &TemplatesGetQueryRequest {
                versions_per_template: Some(10),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```

## Usage
<details><summary><code>client.usage.<a href="/src/api/resources/usage/usage.rs">get_usage_by_product_over_time</a>(body: &amp;BodyGetWorkspaceUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryUsageByProductOverTimePost, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Returns credit usage broken down by product type over time, for workspaces billed in credits. The response is a tabular structure with columns, column_types, column_units, and rows. Some id columns also get a display-name column, such as user_label or voice_name, appended after the existing columns. For workspaces billed by cost, ranges that reach the date the workspace moved to cost billing return an error; use /v1/workspace/analytics/usage instead.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .usage
        .get_usage_by_product_over_time(
            &BodyGetWorkspaceUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryUsageByProductOverTimePost::builder()
                .start_time(8037220951716727)
                .end_time(5812684333956902)
                .interval_seconds(60)
                .group_by(vec![
                    BodyGetWorkspaceUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryUsageByProductOverTimePostGroupByItem::ProductType,
                ])
                .filters(vec![
                    ColumnFilter::builder()
                        .column("column")
                        .operation(ColumnFilterOperation::In_)
                        .values(vec![])
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                ])
                .time_zone("UTC")
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**body:** `&BodyGetWorkspaceUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryUsageByProductOverTimePost`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>
</dl>


</dd>
</dl>
</details>

<details><summary><code>client.usage.<a href="/src/api/resources/usage/usage.rs">get_usage</a>(body: &amp;BodyGetWorkspaceCostUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsUsagePost, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Returns the cost of the workspace's usage over time, for workspaces billed by cost. Usage is bucketed by UTC day. The response is a tabular structure with columns, column_types, column_units, and rows, with one row per group and bucket. `total_cost` is the cost in the workspace's currency and `total_charge_count` the billed quantity. Usage can be grouped or filtered by at most two of `user_id`, `hashed_xi_api_key`, `region`, `reporting_workspace_id`, `billing_group_id`, `product_type`, `surface` and `actor`, and grouping by two of them requires an `eq` or `in` filter on one. `model`, `request_source`, `fiat_charge_type` and `fiat_currency` can always be added. Some id columns also get a display-name column, such as user_label, appended after the existing columns. Workspaces billed in credits should use /v1/workspace/analytics/query/usage-by-product-over-time.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### 🔌 Usage

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

```rust
use elevenlabs_rust_sdk::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let config = ClientConfig::default();
    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .usage
        .get_usage(
            &BodyGetWorkspaceCostUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsUsagePost::builder()
                .start_time(6170929235327434)
                .end_time(412967195721056.94)
                .interval_seconds(282899197814400)
                .group_by(vec![
                    BodyGetWorkspaceCostUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsUsagePostGroupByItem::Model,
                ])
                .filters(vec![
                    MetronomeUsageColumnFilter::builder()
                        .column(
                            BodyGetWorkspaceCostUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsUsagePostGroupByItem::Model,
                        )
                        .operation(MetronomeUsageColumnFilterOperation::Eq)
                        .values(vec![])
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                ])
                .build()
                .expect("Failed to build request"),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
```
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

#### ⚙️ Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

**body:** `&BodyGetWorkspaceCostUsageV1WorkspaceAnalyticsUsagePost`
    
</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

**options:** `Option<RequestOptions>` — Per-call overrides
    
</dd>
</dl>

</dd>

<details><summary><code>client.requests.<a href="/src/api/resources/requests/requests.rs">get</a>(body: Option&lt;&amp;BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPost&gt;, options: Option&lt;RequestOptions&gt;) -&gt; Result&lt;WorkspaceAnalyticsQueryResponseModel, crate::error::ApiError&gt;</code></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

#### 📝 Description

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>
<dd>

Returns a list of API requests. Supports filtering by time range, column filters, and search terms. At least one of start_time or end_time must be provided. An optional sort parameter controls timestamp ordering. Results are ordered by timestamp. Descending if end_time is used, ascending if start_time is used. The response is a tabular structure with columns, column_types, column_units, and rows.
</dd>
</dl>
</dd>
</dl>

<dd>

    let client = ApiClient::new(config).expect("Failed to build client");
    client
        .requests
        .get(
            Some(&BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPost {
                start_time: Some(1116278011159287),
                end_time: Some(1550763970224527),
                limit: Some(100),
                sort: Some(BodyListApiRequestsV1WorkspaceAnalyticsRequestsPostSort::Asc),
                filters: Some(vec![
                    ColumnFilter::builder()
                        .column("column")
                        .operation(ColumnFilterOperation::In_)
                        .values(vec![])
                        .build()
                        .expect("Failed to build request"),
                ]),
                search: Some("search".to_string()),
                ..Default::default()
            }),
            None,
        )
        .await;
}
